description: Width tiers for Languages — Background Language Learner Entry Pathway, Years 7–8
subject: Languages — Background Language Learner Entry

width_notes.minimum_width: The narrowest honest floor for the descriptor's command term at Y7-8 entry level. Entry pathway students bring significant home and community language experience but are encountering structured school-based target language learning for the first time. Minimum reflects what every entry student must demonstrate, not what is easy.
width_notes.typical_width: The full descriptor scope from ACARA elaborations — what a well-taught Y7-8 background entry class would have engaged with across the breadth of the descriptor.
width_notes.wider: Enrichment directions that add new task contexts (communicating/creating) or new language/cultural phenomena (understanding). Entry students' authentic home-language and community experience is a primary width resource — width tasks should activate and extend this.
width_notes.elaborations: ACARA elaborations for the Chinese Background and First Language Learner Entry pathway (Y7-8) used as source data. (BL) annotations in source refer to Background Language learner sub-tasks; (L1) to First Language learner sub-tasks. Both are treated as representative elaboration examples.

AC9LCH8EC01.minimum_width: Initiate and sustain an exchange using culturally appropriate conventions for at least four turns including at least one expression of preference or opinion; produce at least one digital or written interaction text using appropriate format conventions.
AC9LCH8EC01.typical_width: Initiate and sustain conversations about personal interests, hobbies and future plans in culturally appropriate ways; express preferences with justifications; ensure inclusion of other participants; respond with agreement or disagreement; maintain contact via digital platforms; exchange information about special events and community celebrations; respond appropriately to invitations.
wider: Compare culturally appropriate conversation initiation and participation conventions in the target language with Australian English — identify specific differences in how inclusion, agreement and disagreement are managed
Create a bilingual digital interaction text for a dual-language audience — selecting language for each section based on audience and purpose
Participate in an extended exchange with a peer from a target language community through a secure digital platform — documenting communication strategies used and reflecting on their effectiveness
elaborations: initiating and sustaining conversations in a culturally appropriate way to share personal interests such as hobbies and future plans
clarifying or paraphrasing the teacher's instructions when needed and responding to questions
expressing preferences, stating reasons and making sure other participants are included
engaging in class discussion by responding to questions and expressing agreement or disagreement in a culturally appropriate way
exchanging emails using appropriate format and modelled language highlighting school, home or social activities
responding to invitations to participate in personal celebrations, including accepting and declining appropriately
sharing information with peers in target language communities in face-to-face and secure online conversations
maintaining contact with friends or peers and recording events in everyday life through a secure online journal or blog
exchanging information about special events or community celebrations

AC9LCH8EC02.minimum_width: Contribute at least two planning decisions in target language to a collaborative project; participate in at least one transactional exchange using target language to negotiate a detail and reach a conclusion; create at least one bilingual resource with accurate meaning transfer for a community audience.
AC9LCH8EC02.typical_width: Plan target language cultural days and community events; make and simulate transactions including bargaining and itinerary planning; organise class or school celebrations explaining cultural practices; produce bilingual promotional materials; collaborate on school projects comparing Australian and target language education systems; provide metalanguage-supported peer feedback.
wider: Lead the planning of a community cultural event — coordinating decisions, managing peer input, and driving the group to an outcome using target language
Create a bilingual resource for a real community need and evaluate it with a target audience member — revising based on feedback
Design a group project comparing aspects of education or daily life in Australia and a target language region — drawing on personal research and own cultural experience
elaborations: planning a Chinese cultural day to support cultural diversity within the school or local community
collaborating to create displays, presentations or performances to showcase learning
producing bilingual versions of promotional materials to assist the target language community to engage with school activities
making real or simulated transactions such as purchasing goods or planning an itinerary
negotiating with peers about potential purchases based on collective opinions
designing an 'ideal school' in groups using research and own experiences to compare education in Australia and target language regions
organising a class or school celebration explaining cultural practices and comparing with practices in other communities
providing feedback using metalanguage to support peers
creating resources to help others such as helpful hints for school

AC9LCH8EC03.minimum_width: Apply at least two comprehension strategies across different text types and locate key information from at least one spoken and one written text; evaluate at least two target language digital sources using at least one credibility criterion.
AC9LCH8EC03.typical_width: Listen for key facts in spoken texts using note-taking strategies; access and evaluate digital and print sources; gather information using target language search tools; keep a reading journal for imaginative texts; respond to First Nations Australian stories in target language; express personal opinions on social media and traditional texts.
wider: Access and compare target language and English language sources on the same topic — compare the perspectives available and discuss how the source language shapes the information
Evaluate a set of digital sources systematically — categorise by type, purpose and reliability, and justify source selection for a specific research purpose
Listen to or read a First Nations Australian author's story in English and take notes of key details in target language — write a summary or report in the target language
elaborations: listening for key facts in spoken or recorded texts and using note-taking strategies
listening to official broadcasts and identifying key points and interpreting implications
accessing information related to own experiences as target language students in Australia
listening to or reading First Nations Australian authors' stories in English and taking notes or writing a summary in the target language
gathering information about aspects of target language regions and using information in new ways
accessing a range of digital and other texts to collate and present information about Chinese and Australian topics
evaluating possible print or digital resources before undertaking a research project
viewing extracts from various sources and expressing personal opinions
reading a range of imaginative texts and keeping a reading journal

AC9LCH8EC04.minimum_width: Convert at least one informal expression into formal register; interpret at least one exchange demonstrating at least one clarifying or cultural explanation strategy; produce at least one bilingual text with accurate meaning transfer and at least one deliberate translation decision.
AC9LCH8EC04.typical_width: Use formal register appropriate to context; identify cultural connotations of words expressing emotion; act as interpreter applying clarifying and rephrasing strategies; apply strategies to translate culturally-embedded idioms; read bilingual texts and identify untranslatable expressions; produce bilingual texts; use dictionaries and digital tools for translation support.
wider: Apply translation strategies to rewrite lyrics, story lines or procedures in the target language — documenting each decision and evaluating the result
Compare own informal community interpreting experience with the structured strategies introduced — identify what is already intuitive and what requires explicit development
Interpret the main theme of target language poems or songs — explain key messages and cultural context with reference to own background knowledge
elaborations: using language to reflect formality appropriate to context
discussing cultural connotations of words that express emotion
acting as interpreter for visitors applying strategies such as clarifying, rephrasing and explaining
applying strategies to translate idioms, fables or stories that cannot be translated directly
reading bilingual children's stories and identifying expressions that cannot be translated directly
producing own bilingual texts to help target language peers understand course content
using a range of resources to assist in creating a target language translation
interpreting the main theme of target language poems or songs
identifying features of communication that are interpreted differently across languages
applying translation strategies and rewriting lyrics or story lines in the target language

AC9LCH8EC05.minimum_width: Create at least one informative text using appropriate textual conventions with at least one supporting visual element; create at least one imaginative text with at least one deliberate creative choice and at least one cultural reference.
AC9LCH8EC05.typical_width: Create digital presentations with sound, voice and music; produce posters and brochures for cultural events; write journal entries and school newsletter contributions; create subtitles for video clips; compose songs, jingles or video clips; write and perform role-plays using cultural stories; create texts depicting experiences of target language community members in Australia.
wider: Create texts depicting experiences of target language-speaking people in Australia — for example, a short interview with an older community member about their life in Australia
Create and perform an original role-play using alternative versions of cultural stories, incorporating voice, rhythm and gesture to animate characters
Create a multimodal text for a real external audience — evaluate its effectiveness with that audience and revise based on feedback
elaborations: creating digital presentations adding sound, voice and music
producing a poster or digital brochure for a cultural event
creating texts depicting experiences of target language-speaking people in Australia
writing a journal entry or contributing to a school newsletter reflecting on a school excursion
developing material to explain a procedure or practice such as a recipe or tutorial
creating subtitles to match short video clips of intercultural experiences
composing songs, jingles or video clips to promote real or imagined products
writing and performing role-plays using alternative versions of cultural stories
creating an original story based on modelled expressions or idioms from traditional literature

AC9LCH8EU01.minimum_width: Explain how the phonetic system represents spoken sounds and use it to check pronunciation of at least three characters; identify at least two homophone pairs and describe a strategy for discriminating between them; compare own speech with a standard model and identify at least two specific differences.
AC9LCH8EU01.typical_width: Explore key features of target language phonology; use Pinyin to generate digital texts and support pronunciation; discriminate between homophones; compare own speech with Modern Standard target language in broadcasts; identify subtle pronunciation differences and regional accents; perform poems with rhythm, voice and gesture; prepare speeches with support from target language community members.
wider: Research the regional accent features of own family or community variety — describe specific phonological patterns and explain their geographic origin
Prepare a mock lesson for beginner language students about target language phonology — explaining the system clearly for someone who has never encountered it
Compare own pronunciation with target language spoken in different regional communities — identify systematic differences and discuss what they reveal
elaborations: exploring key features of target language phonology, examining the range of sounds
recognising the value of Pinyin romanisation to assist in distinguishing differences in spoken language
recognising and discriminating between homophones and enhancing fluency through tongue twisters
identifying subtle differences in pronunciation in own and others' speech such as regional accents
comparing own speech to pronunciation in Modern Standard target language such as news broadcasts
performing poems and experimenting with rhythm, voice, emotion and gesture
using dictionaries or digital tools to check correct pronunciation of unknown characters
preparing a mock lesson for beginner students about target language phonology
preparing a speech in target language and practising with family or peers

AC9LCH8EU02.minimum_width: Identify components of at least five characters with explanation of their contribution; write at least five characters with correct stroke order; produce at least three sentences using different sentence types with correct punctuation.
AC9LCH8EU02.typical_width: Identify nature, arrangement and function of components; identify radical placement patterns; apply stroke direction and order; explore running script or cursive forms; use digital tools for unknown characters; join, contrast and sequence using cohesive devices; construct sentences in affirmative, negative, interrogative and imperative forms; compare simplified and traditional character forms.
wider: Investigate a semantic component family — all characters sharing a specific radical — and explain the semantic or phonetic pattern connecting them
Analyse own extended writing for accuracy — identify patterns of error relating to stroke order, component identification, or syntactic structure, and develop a targeted revision plan
Explore the relationship between running script or cursive forms and standard printed forms — discuss what changes and what the relationship tells us about the history of the writing system
elaborations: identifying the nature of components, and their arrangement and function in a range of characters
inferring characters and meanings in phrases representing auspicious meanings
applying rules of stroke direction and stroke order when writing characters
using digital tools to write unknown characters and assist with stroke order
identifying the possible placement of specific radicals and components in compound characters
examining the relationship between characters in a word to identify subtle differences in meaning
recognising differences between characters of similar appearance
analysing how words containing a common morpheme are related
using punctuation conventions to express different meanings
joining, contrasting and sequencing using cohesive devices
constructing sentences in affirmative, negative, interrogative and imperative forms
differentiating characters based on the meanings of each morpheme
comparing known simplified characters with traditional characters and discussing differences

AC9LCH8EU03.minimum_width: Use at least five metalanguage terms correctly in comparing at least two grammatical features across target language and English; analyse the structure of at least one text type in both languages identifying at least three differences.
AC9LCH8EU03.typical_width: Use metalanguage to compare grammar across languages; compare ways of sequencing ideas for different audiences; read target language texts and select and explain appealing language choices; read formal texts and compare with everyday speech; compare expressions of ideas across traditional and contemporary literary texts.
wider: Create a teaching resource about a specific language difference between the target language and English — test with a real or simulated learner audience and revise based on feedback
Compare the expression of ideas in diverse traditional and contemporary literary target language texts — identify how cultural values and conventions have or have not changed across time
Apply comparative metalanguage knowledge to analyse a genuinely unfamiliar text type — document strategies used and evaluate their effectiveness
elaborations: discussing aspects of grammar, using metalanguage in Chinese or English
comparing different ways of sequencing ideas for different audiences and purposes
reading texts and choosing expressions or sentences that appeal and explaining choices
reading samples of formal texts and identifying how language compares with everyday speech
comparing the expression of ideas in diverse traditional and contemporary literary texts

AC9LCH8EU04.minimum_width: Identify at least two examples of cultural values reflected in target language use with explanation; reflect on at least two ways different language or cultural communities have shaped own identity; explain at least one communicative practice that may be misinterpreted across cultures.
AC9LCH8EU04.typical_width: Discuss identity and cultural values in language and gesture; compare cultural differences across target language regions; explain communicative practices interpreted differently across cultures; examine First Nations Australian language connections to Country; reflect on how humour works differently across cultures; explore own cultural identity through language choices and community involvement.
wider: Examine in target language or English how First Nations Australians' languages have strong connections to Country/Place and compare with how the target language connects to cultural community and belonging
Interview a family member or community elder about their language and cultural identity — compare their experience with own and discuss what has changed across generations

Conduct a comparative analysis of humour across the target language and Australian English — explain what is shared and what is culturally specific and what the comparison reveals about cultural values
elaborations: discussing identity and cultural values reflected in language use and how they influence interactions
comparing key differences between target language speaking regions and considering cultural diversity
explaining communicative practices that might be perceived differently in different cultures
examining in Chinese or English how First Nations Australians' languages have strong connections to Country/Place
identifying ways in which Chinese identity is reflected in own values, beliefs and language
exploring how known languages influence own way of communicating
identifying elements of own community and identity including involvement in cultural practices
reading jokes or cartoons in Chinese and discussing how humour is conveyed
discussing experiences of living in a target language country and comparing lifestyles and practices
